assumptions: Hosts keep exporting OTLP HTTP/JSON and posting hooks as documented on 2026-10-31; the Claude desktop browser pane loads loopback pages; the viewer runs on the same machine as the hosts; ADR 0032 and ADR 0033 are decided before implementation.
compatibility: New contract agent-braid-loom/v0.1, new effort pack contract agent-braid-loom-effort-pack/v0.1, new surfaces matrix agent-braid-view-surfaces/v0.1 and new optional command group agent-braid view. No change to existing contracts, the plugin package, the portable MCP surface, the SPEC-047 telemetry store or frozen evidence. Vendored Three.js adds an MIT directory under ADR 0033.
domain: Local machine, loopback interface, Agent Braid artifacts of the current contracts (analysis, Git replay plan, scheduler preparations, runtime grants and state, SPEC-057 ownership outputs as JSON, SPEC-052 gate results, host stream events) and Claude Code and Codex telemetry shapes recorded in fixtures. Not covered: transcripts, cloud sessions, IDE extensions, other hosts.
execution_contract: Read-only. No route, command or control executes, schedules, grants, retries, cancels or writes to repositories, registries, run directories or host configuration; executionAuthorization is the constant false; network use is limited to a loopback server; effort data stays in memory; writes only to explicit export destinations.
hypotheses: H-VIS1 (not a requirement): seeing the braid shortens the time an operator needs to locate a hazard or conflicting pair compared with reading the JSON receipt. Null or inconclusive results are valid.
observation_contract: Owned fixtures and recorded host payloads; byte comparison of adapter outputs against source artifacts; HTTP requests against a loopback test server; file-system snapshots for persistence checks; host behavior only through owner-run receipts recorded separately with environment and limits.

scenarios.given: the schema and a corpus of valid and seeded invalid events
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure_001 record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: valid lines pass and every line with an unknown kind, a missing or non-false `executionAuthorization`, a crossing without an integer class, an effort event with a class, a status outside its source enum, an `evidenceRef` path that is absolute or contains `..`, a non-increasing `seq`, duplicate JSON members, a non-finite number or an oversized line is refused with a stable reason and no partial acceptance.

requirements.text: Versioned event contract: Every event is one JSON object per line with `schemaVersion` `agent-braid-loom/v0.1`, a strictly increasing integer `seq`, a `kind` from a closed list, a relative monotonic time `at` (`relMs`, `basis`), a `source` (`adapter`, `evidenceRef`, `host`), an `assurance` block (`compatibilityClass`, `notAGuarantee: true`) and `executionAuthorization` fixed to `false`. `compatibilityClass` is the Article 13 class declared by the analysis fact an event carries and is `null` for events that carry no analysis result (strands, effort, gaps, session). The closed kinds are `session.origin`, `analysis.report`, `strand.open`, `strand.update`, `strand.close`, `crossing.classified`, `wave.planned`, `wave.started`, `wave.finished`, `grant.issued`, `grant.consumed`, `grant.expired`, `grant.refused`, `hazard.noticed`, `gate.phase`, `gate.result`, `runtime.phase`, `effort.sample` and `observation.gap`. Status and mode values are copied verbatim from their source contracts. Lines are at most 16 KiB. A file or POST body with more than 50 000 events is refused; the live in-memory ring instead evicts old events and announces each evicted range (REQ-006). The schema and an illustrative example are in [contracts/](contracts/).

scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure_002 record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: both outputs are byte-identical, every crossing equals one pair of the source analysis with the same classification, shared resources, evidence block and class, every status equals its source value, every event's `evidenceRef` hash matches the artifact, and a static import check finds no ownership import in any viewer module.

requirements.text: Artifact adapters bound to evidence: Deterministic adapters translate, without recomputing or reinterpreting them: analysis reports (report-level summary, uncertainty and limits; per pair the classification, shared resources, reasons, constraints, evidence method, coverage, rule set and compatibility class), Git replay plans, scheduler preparations (waves and workers), runtime grants and phases, ownership pre-flight notices and receipts read as JSON files, workflow-gate results and host stream events (`claude -p` stream-json, `codex exec --json`). Each event carries an `evidenceRef` (artifact path relative to its declared root, plus a SHA-256 of the artifact bytes). Events the viewer derives rather than reads (a grant expiry observed after its recorded validity) carry `derived: true`. Viewer modules do not import `agent_braid.ownership` and contain no ownership command name.

requirements.text: Absence never looks clean: `unknown` classifications, `not-observed` hazards, partial coverage, unparsed host shapes, truncated streams and ring eviction are carried as events and rendered distinctly from independent or clean results. `observation.gap` reasons form a closed list: `subagent-usage-unattributed`, `stream-truncated`, `shape-unpinned`, `ring-evicted`, `host-unverified`, `not-observed`.

requirements.text: Loopback server boundary: `agent-braid view serve` binds only to `127.0.0.1` (or `::1`), prints a random per-session token and serves every route under that token. Requests with a non-loopback `Host` or `Origin`, a wrong token, an oversized body, a wrong content type, duplicate JSON members or non-finite numbers are refused with the statuses in the [UI, security and privacy contract](contracts/ui-security-privacy.md#refusal-statuses). Responses carry the contract's Content Security Policy with no remote origins. The server exposes no route that executes, schedules, grants, writes to a repository or changes host configuration. Limits: 256 strands, 4 096 crossings, 64 waves, 1 024 grants, 8 concurrent subscribers; OTLP bodies at most 1 MiB and hook bodies at most 256 KiB.

scenarios.given: recorded payload fixtures for each host shape, including payloads carrying prompt text, tool output and unknown attributes
scenarios.planned_evidence: Candidate-bound procedure_005 record: command, hashes, environment, expected and actual outcome, negative controls and limits.
scenarios.then: only allowlisted attributes keep values in events, no dropped value is present in the store, in any response or in any export, unknown attribute names appear only in the names inventory, identifiers differ between two server sessions, and unknown shapes produce a `shape-unpinned` gap.

requirements.text: Live host ingest with an attribute allowlist: The server accepts OTLP HTTP/JSON logs and metrics (Claude Code `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY` export; Codex `[otel]` export), Claude Code HTTP hook payloads and Codex `notify` or hook-shim posts. Only the attributes of the canonical allowlist in the [UI, security and privacy contract](contracts/ui-security-privacy.md#data-minimization) keep their values. Identifiers are replaced by values salted per server session. Prompt text, message text, tool input, tool output and file content are dropped before storage. The names (never values) of dropped attributes are kept in a bounded in-memory inventory for host verification. An unrecognized shape yields `observation.gap` `shape-unpinned` instead of a guess.

requirements.text: Replay and live delivery: The same viewer consumes a recorded loom file (`--replay`) and the live store. Server-Sent Events resume from `Last-Event-ID`; evicted events are announced by a `ring-evicted` gap; `/snapshot` returns the current state. Artifact directories named with `--watch` are polled with fixed bounds: at most 8 roots, 4 096 files, 16 MiB read per file, known artifact names only, every 500 ms.

requirements.text: Ephemeral effort and explicit recording: Effort data (tokens, cost, durations) lives in process memory, is labeled `basis: host-estimate`, uses relative monotonic time and is never written to the SPEC-047 telemetry store or to a repository. `serve` writes nothing unless the user passes `--record FILE`, which writes the loom stream to a new private file outside repositories (destination rules of REQ-008); effort events are recorded only with the additional flag `--record-effort`.

requirements.text: Explicit, minimal export: `agent-braid view export --from FILE --to PATH` reads a recorded or replay loom file and writes to a new private destination outside repositories, refusing existing, symlinked, repository or public destinations as in SPEC-043. By default it omits `effort.sample` events and absolute paths. Output is deterministic for the same input.

requirements.text: Comparative effort evidence pack: With `--include-effort` and two or more `--arm NAME=FILE` recordings made with `--record-effort`, export adds per-strand and per-phase effort, a summary and a static HTML/SVG rendering without scripts or remote resources. Comparisons are pairwise between a named baseline arm and each other arm. The pack records how each arm was selected, states that arms are unmatched unless the owner records a matching, and compares only fields present in both arms. Comparison rows use the row shape of `agent-braid harness compare` (`field`, `left`, `right`), with `identical` and `unlistedChange` at comparison level. Every figure is labeled `host-estimate` and `empirical` and carries no compatibility class; the pack states that it is not a speedup, saving or causal claim. Registering the pack as a Braid Harness record kind is a HAR decision outside VIS.1. The contract is in [contracts/effort-evidence-pack.md](contracts/effort-evidence-pack.md).

requirements.text: Web viewer bound to facts: The viewer renders strands, crossings, waves, grants, gates, hazards, effort and gaps following the visual grammar in [research.md](research.md#visual-grammar). Every visible element maps to one event; selecting it shows the event, its compatibility class as a categorical label, shared resources, evidence method, coverage, reasons, constraints, the report's uncertainty and limits, and the `evidenceRef`. Only `independent-candidate` pairs are drawn as strand swaps; ordered, conflicting and unknown pairs have their own glyphs and never look like a clean swap; strands that pass between non-adjacent lanes are drawn as visibly uncrossed bridges. Classes are shown categorically, never as a safety ordering, and the legend states that a class is not a guarantee. Counters show only measures the events support: conflicts flagged, ordered pairs, independent candidates, unknown pairs, planned wave width against the serial fallback (advisory, not verified safe), hazards, gaps, gates and grants. No counter shows speedup. Lane ordering is a layout choice and never a braid simplification. Three.js is vendored at a pinned version with a hash manifest; first-party files reference no remote origin and the bundle performs no remote load. A text table view of the same model is available without WebGL.

scientific_limits: Engineering specification. The braid picture is a representation of computed classifications, not a braid-theoretic result; no braid relation or simplification is applied. Effort figures are empirical host estimates without a compatibility class, and support no speedup, cost-saving or causal claim. H-VIS1 is an unobserved hypothesis; an optional owner-run observation would be small, unblinded and descriptive. Structural checks are not owner approval.
scope: VIS.1 read-only, loopback-only activity viewer companion: event contract agent-braid-loom/v0.1, artifact adapters, OTLP/JSON and hook ingest for Claude Code and Codex, in-memory store, Server-Sent Events, replay, Three.js web viewer, pure frames, minimal export and opt-in comparative effort evidence pack. Specification only; VIS.2-VIS.4 are derived tracks.
